prompt: Write a recorded statement transcript (about 250 words) between an insurance adjuster (lines start with 'Q:') and the claimant (lines start with 'A:'). The claimant was the driver in a rear-end collision in Pasadena, Texas, and has whiplash. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1107; do not mention it.)
text:
Q: Thanks for taking the time to speak with me today. This call is being recorded. Please state your full name for the record.

A: I'd rather not give my full name on a recording, but you can use the claim number.

Q: That works. Can you tell me where you were when the collision happened?

A: I was driving on a main road in Pasadena, Texas, heading toward the shopping center. Traffic had slowed down at a light, and I came to a stop behind a gray sedan.

Q: What happened next?

A: I was stopped for maybe five seconds when I felt a hard jolt from behind. My head snapped forward and then back against the headrest. My car got pushed into the sedan in front of me.

Q: Did you see the vehicle that hit you before the impact?

A: No. I was looking at the light and my mirrors didn't show anything close. I only heard tires squeal a split second before it hit.

Q: Did you get out of the vehicle and speak with the other driver?

A: Yes, briefly. He said he looked down at his phone and didn't see that traffic had stopped. He seemed shaken but okay.

Q: How are you feeling now?

A: My neck is stiff and sore, and it hurts when I turn my head to the left. I also have a headache that starts at the base of my skull. I went to urgent care and they said it looked like whiplash. I have a follow-up with my doctor next week.

Q: Have you missed any work because of the injury?

A: A few shifts so far. I'm still deciding whether I can handle lifting and driving for long periods.

Q: Is there anything else you think I should know?

A: Only that I was wearing my seatbelt and I was not using my phone at the time. I'm willing to provide my medical records.

Q: Thank you. I'll follow up with you once I have reviewed everything.
